actionable_steps.step: Look upon whatever you receive today as a gift from God — be satisfied with what you have and what you get.
For the disease of insatiable desires, apply the remedy of thripti — refuse to feed the next craving.
Have contentment whatever the gain or loss; desire only the Lord, not the mean desires of the world.
Speak sweetly — let your words spread contentment and joy, not wounds that fester.
Curb the craving for fashion and show; use your time as the precious gift of God it is.

definition.quote: Na santhoshathparam sukham (There is no happiness greater than contentment). Contentment, it is said, confers the greatest happiness.

discourses.quote: A contented man is happier than a millionaire. The poorest man in the world is the one who has insatiable desires. Be content with what you get and carry on your duties.
At this stage man must learn to be content with what he has and what he gets and look upon whatever he receives as gift from God. When he is satisfied with what he has, he can be happy.

discourses.citation: Disciplines of the spirit — SSS Vol 22 (1989), 1989-09-03
discourses.quote: Man can experience joy and happiness only when he has contentment. As desires grow, discontent grows and worries multiply. You must learn to be content with your condition. He who has got much satisfaction is the richest man.

discourses.citation: Food, the heart and the mind — SSS Vol 27 (1994), 1994-01-21
discourses.quote: What is the cause of this worry? Lack of contentment is the cause. The rich man is not contented in spite of the accumulation of wealth.

make_it_real: A contented man is happier than a millionaire — today, count your blessings, not your lacks.
title: Contentment

vahinis.quote: If there is contentment in the mind, one enjoys an endless festival. Craving makes the mind waver; it is an all-consuming fire that will destroy people slowly and surely. The royal road to meditation is contentment.

The contented person is free and does not depend upon others. The person is unaffected by the feeling of doership and is content with whatever happens, well or ill, for the contented person is convinced that the Lord's will must prevail.
